Description: Percentage of staff turnover
Variation: Reduced turnover rate due to temporary staff roles being replaced by permanent positions.

Description: Cost of library service per population
Variation: The cost of the library service per head of population is marginally lower than the previous year. This is a direct result of continuous improvement initiatives designed to deliver greater value to the Monash community.

Description: Health inspections of aquatic facilities
Variation: Health inspections were undertaken on all three facilities (one per site).

Description: Utilisation of aquatic facilities
Variation: Total attendances up by more than 37% (continued recovery from COVID and increase in program numbers and Oakleigh Recreation Centre visitations).

Description: Cost of aquatic facilities
Variation: Operating costs were higher than budget, due to higher staffing costs, utilities and maintenance costs in the first six months of the financial year. However, corrective action was applied to reduce the cost of aquatic facilities in the second half of the year with a particular focus in casual wages and increasing member and program numbers as normal operation resumes.

Description: Time taken to action animal management requests
Variation: The response time improved by 15% compared to the previous 12-month period.   This can be largely attributed to an increase in the number of available officers enabling a more consistent response throughout the year.

Description: Animals reclaimed
Variation: In comparison to 2022/23, the last 12 months has seen a 12% reduction in the number of animals collected, while the number of reclaimed animals remained at a similar level. While this resulted in a 9% improvement in the overall reclaim rate, the trend of dogs returning a high reclaim rate continues, as does the low reclaim rate for cats.

Description: Animals rehomed
Variation: The rehoming rate for 2023/24 has increased significantly compared to the prior years as the measure for the current year has changed and looks at the number of unclaimed animals that have been rehomed. There has been significant industry focus and initiatives on animal rehoming which has led to maintaining positive reclaim rates, along with the strong appeal of adopting cats, which sits around 80% compared to the reclaim rate of 13%.

Description: Cost of animal management service per population
Variation: The last 12 months continued to experience the increasing trend in animal pound costs, resulting in an overall increase of 9% in the delivery of the service per population. The added influence to this outcome, includes the cost of additional staff resources and associated equipment required to meet growing operational demands.

Description: Animal management prosecutions
Variation: Council continues to achieve a 100% success rate in prosecutions (9 prosecutions this year). The continued high success rate in prosecutions is reflective of the willingness of people to report incidents that impact wider community safety and amenity, which is complemented by the quality of investigations and enforcement skills within the relevant teams.

Description: Time taken to action food complaints
Variation: This represents the 2023 calendar year, as per the performance reporting requirements. All non-conformances have been followed up and this is consistent with previous years.

Description: Food safety assessments
Variation: This result represents the 2023 calendar year, as per the performance reporting requirements. Council has consistently demonstrated diligence in conducting food safety assessments for food businesses. Of those food premises that require a food safety assessment, seven were not able to be assessed due to being closed and not in operation during the reporting period.

Description: Cost of food safety service
Variation: The overall average cost of service has marginally increased in comparison to previous years, largely due to costs associated with staffing.

Description: Critical and major non-compliance outcome notifications
Variation: This represents the 2023 calendar year, as per the performance reporting requirements. All 287 non-conformances have been followed up and this is consistent with previous years.

Description: Food safety samples
Variation: This represents the 2023 calendar year, as per the performance reporting requirements. The number of food samples obtained exceeded the number of samples required under legislation, demonstrating Council's commitment to food safety surveillance.

Description: Council decisions made at meetings closed to the public
Variation: Council saw an increase in the number of confidential resolutions, due to an increase in property related matters. These types of matters are appropriately confidential under section 3(1)(c) of the Local Government Act.

Description: Satisfaction with community consultation and engagement
Variation: Satisfaction with Council’s community consultation and engagement performance remained at “good” levels, but did see a slight decrease this year, from 72 to 71.

Description: Councillor attendance at council meetings
Variation: There has been an overall decrease in Councillor attendance at meetings, with an increase in attendance during the second half the year.

Description: Cost of elected representation
Variation: The costs include training, conferences, seminars, memberships, IT and the provision of facilities. The majority is attributed to Councillor allowances, as set by the Victorian Independent Remuneration Tribunal. This year it includes both a reviewed increase and CPI increase.

Description: Satisfaction with council decisions
Variation: Satisfaction with Council’s performance making decisions in the interest of the community remained at “good” levels, but did see a slight decrease this year, from 72 to 71. This still places Monash above the metropolitan Melbourne results of 69 (Metropolis Research 2024, Governing Melbourne).

Description: Recently purchased library collection
Variation: A significant effort and investment within existing budgets have been made to ensure the library collections reflect the needs and interests of our library members and local community.

Description: Loans per head of population
Variation: Loans per head of population exceeded the target of 7.5 to finish at 7.8 at the end of year, reflective of an increased membership base.

Description: Library membership
Variation: A new measure from the last reporting period capturing active membership. A drive to increase the overall total number of registered members, resulted in an increase of our membership baseline number.

Description: Library visits per head of population
Variation: The number of visits per head of population exceeded its target of 3.0 to finish on 3.87 in this reporting year and reflects not only borrowers but also participants in programs, students studying etc.

Description: Infant enrolments in the MCH service
Variation: Monash had a minor increase in birth notifications received. The greater than 100% result in the MC2.1 can be related to infants who have been enrolled into this years' Maternal and Child Health service but were born in the previous financial year (just prior to year-end).

Description: Cost of the MCH service
Variation: Decrease in cost of Maternal Child Health service. The Maternal and Child Health service has been able to offer an increased number of service hours to support the Maternal and Child Health program with increased casual staff available.

Description: Participation in the MCH service
Variation:
Nursing recruitment has impacted the Maternal and Child Health service delivery over the past 12 months. The sector-wide workforce shortage has reduced appointment capacity, impacting the number of clients able to be seen. Key Age and Stage (KAS) appointment focus has centred around improving continuity of care for families and focused on the early visits. 

Workforce planning has been implemented to support future service delivery across all Maternal and Child Health programs.

Description: Participation in the MCH service by Aboriginal children
Variation:
Reduction in the number of First Nations children seen in Maternal and Child Health this year (40 attendances). 

Analysis of the data shows acceptable Maternal and Child Health early attendance results in FY23, indicating an uptake of 88% of First Nations families attending at least once. Reduced attendance for later visits is in line with reduced attendance of non-First Nations families of the same age. The small numbers of Aboriginal children means that a slight variation in visits by any family can affect the data.

The Maternal and Child Health service continue to undertake cultural competency training and implementation of this training into daily practice.

Description: Participation in 4-week Key Age and Stage visit
Variation:
Slight decrease in attendance at the 4-week Key Age and Stage (KAS) although 96% is still a strong result. Maternal and Child Health service has implemented a strong continuity of service plan to support families to see the same Maternal and Child Health nurse across their service delivery. The continuity of care model will assist attendance across all KAS appointments and strengthening attendance. 

Monash also saw an increase of clients transferring out of Monash to other municipalities during this year, impacting attendance at KAS appointments when compared to birth notices received.

Description: Sealed local road requests
Variation: The number of local road requests has decreased compared to the previous reporting period. This is despite the fact that the number of requests is reflective of wetter conditions on our sealed roads, experienced during the last few years. Wet weather generally leads to higher instances of issues, such as potholes. Council addresses these requests in line with intervention levels, as per our Road Management Plan.

Description: Sealed local roads maintained to condition standards
Variation: Programming of road resurfacing has increasingly been better planned. Council's continuous commitment to invest in the renewal of its road network has kept the number of roads classified as "very poor condition" to a low number.

Description: Cost of sealed local road reconstruction
Variation: The road reconstruction cost has remained steady with the previous reporting period. Three reconstruction projects were completed during this period.

Description: Cost of sealed local road resealing
Variation:
The cost per square metre of road resealing has increased compared to 2022/23. The unit rate tends to fluctuate year to year, based upon the works undertaken on various road hierarchy, minimum tonnages of asphalt placed on each road location, reseal area, night works surcharge, fluctuating petroleum price and the level of traffic management required. 

The increase in the rate during this reporting period is attributed to the treatment of a large section of collector road with a thicker asphalt layer, which led to elevated costs for traffic management, materials, labor and equipment.

Description: Satisfaction with sealed local roads
Variation: The slight decline in the satisfaction with the sealed local roads is attributed to a number of factors including, increased traffic on roads, parking issues, population changes and planning.

Description: Time taken to decide planning applications
Variation: The ongoing improvement in results and the enduring impact of improved work practices implemented in previous years are encouraging signs of progress. The downward trend in processing times from the 2020 to 2024 reporting periods, further underscores the Council's commitment to streamlining procedures and optimizing performance.

Description: Planning applications decided within required time frames
Variation: Council’s percentage for on-time decisions has remained consistent from the prior year and remains high compared to previous years.  The result highlights the continued focus on timely decision making and quality of decisions.  Council continues to review processes in view of continuous improvement and efficient decision making.

Description: Cost of statutory planning service
Variation: As the service costs fluctuates, it's observed that application volume plays a crucial role in determining expenses. A decline in the number of applications, especially those of significant scale, often leads to an increase in the cost per service. Understanding these trends is essential for strategic planning and financial forecasting in any service-driven industry.

Description: Council planning decisions upheld at VCAT
Variation: There has been a significant improvement of 15% to the results when compared to the 2022/2023 reporting period. We have found that during the cost of living crisis, the financial pressures on developers means that they are more willing to negotiate a suitable outcome during the compulsory conference rather than go to a full hearing. Our appeal numbers have also dropped.

Description: Kerbside collection bins missed
Variation: The number of missed bins continues to reduce, with a 40% reduction year-on-year. This can be attributed to best practice contract management and a concerted effort from our waste contractor to meet their performance KPI's.

Description: Cost of kerbside garbage bin collection service
Variation: Further savings derived from increased diversion from landfill have resulted in a cost reduction of 27% year-on-year for general rubbish.

Description: Cost of kerbside recyclables collection service
Variation: Cost of recyclable bin collection has increased, in line with an increase in contract costs.

Description: Kerbside collection waste diverted from landfill
Variation: The positive full year result reflects that Council is performing above target. This is due to the increased take up of Food Organics Garden Organics (FOGO) services by the community and reduction in waste to landfill through the frequency swap.

Description: Expenses per property assessment
Variation: Total expenses increased by 4.2% compared to the previous year. During the year budget approved positions increased employee costs and other temporary resourcing needs were required, in addition to the statutory Superannuation Guarantee Levy that increased from the mandatory 10.5% to 11.0%. A major component of the expenditure increase in materials and services related to the storm event which occurred in February 2024. Extensive damage throughout the municipality especially with trees and reserves resulted in higher costs compared to 2022/23. Insurance costs also increased as well as software support services costs over 2022/23 levels. Future increases in expenditure is expected in line with projected inceases in CPI levels.

Description: Average rate per property assessment
Variation: The rate cap of 3.5% declared by the Minister for Local Government was applied to the 2023/24 rate charges.  This resulted in an increased ratio of 2.7% including an increase in property assessments by 1.0%. Future trends are indicating similar level increases with a projected growth in rates and fluctuations in CPI levels.

Description: Current assets compared to current liabilities
Variation: The liquidity ratio decreased by 22.8% in 2023/24. Current assets decreased by $28.8M. This is mainly due to reductions in cash levels which was invested into the capital works program in 2023/24. This was Council's largest ever capital works program in history.Current liabilities decreased by $4.2M. Cash levels and potential property sales will impact working capital in the initial future years which is expected to smooth to more consistent levels in outer years with a positive trend.

Description: Unrestricted cash compared to current liabilities
Variation: This ratio decreased by 131.5% compared to 2022/23. The variation in this ratio reflects the level of cash held in short term deposits (with maturity dates of 90 Days or less) which is lower by $54.0M compared to the 2022/23 level. This is mainly due to delivering higher capital works program of $109.0M in 2023/24 than in 2022/23.

Description: Loans and borrowings compared to rates
Variation: Council achieved a debt free status as at 30 June 2015. Council does not have any loan borrowings as at 30 June 2024. Future year budgets may require borrowings for various capital works projects but this will be considered and decided upon by Council at the appropriate time.

Description: Loans and borrowings repayments compared to rates
Variation: Council achieved a debt free status as at 30 June 2015. Council does not have any loan borrowings as at 30 June 2024. Future year budgets may require borrowings for various capital works projects but this will be considered and decided upon by Council at the appropriate time.

Description: Non-current liabilities compared to own source revenue
Variation: The 2023/24 ratio compared to the prior year is lower by 14.46%, whilst non-current liabilities have decreased by $0.8M, own source revenue in 2023/24 increased by 7.2%. Statutory Fees and Fines increased compared to 2022/23, particularly with parking infringments which is due to increased patrol services and higher activity in precinct centres. Total user fees increased by $4.1M as leisure, aquatic and other Council facilities returned to full capacity. The trend is indicating a drop due to a forecast reduction in non-current obligations.

Description: Asset renewal and upgrade compared to depreciation
Variation: This ratio has increased by 3.1% on the prior year due to higher renewal and upgrade expenditure undertaken compared to asset depreciation. Council is still meeting its renewal targets and the 207.3% ratio confirms existing high level asset renewal and upgrade expenditure. This is forecast into the next financial year with the continuation of large multi-year projects however future capital works investment drops back to the base renewal program with no provision for major projects.

Description: Adjusted underlying surplus (or deficit)
Variation: The 2023/24 adjusted underlying surplus ratio decreased from -0.5% to -3.4%. Despite recording higher revenue compared with 2022/23, expenditure increased by 5% due to higher employee costs, materials and services cost and depreciation have also contributed to a reduction in the adjusted underlying surplus in 2023/24.

Description: Rates compared to adjusted underlying revenue
Variation: This ratio has increased by 2.1% on the 2022/23 level. Whilst rates are expected to increase according to the rate cap, income from parking fines increased due to revised contractual targets and increased enforcement. User fees increased as leisure, aquatic and other Council facilities returned to full capacity which has contributed to the increased result. The future trend shows consistent results and in line with State Government projected increases in rates and charges.

Description: Rates compared to property values
Variation: The variance reflects Council’s capped rate increase of 3.5% compared to the value of all properties in Monash that decreased by an average 2.8% with the 2024 revaluation.

Description: Expenses per head of municipal population
Variation: The ratio has increased by 0.6% from 2022/23 levels. Total expenses increased by 5.0% compared to 2022/23. During the year budget approved positions increased employee costs and other temporary resourcing needs were required, in addition to the statutory Superannuation Guarantee Levy that increased from the mandatory 10.5% to 11.0%. A major component of the expenditure increase in materials and services related to the storm event which occurred in February 2024. Extensive damage throughout the municipality especially with trees and reserves resulted in higher costs compared to 2022/23. Population increased by 4.5% however with a result of $1,099 indicates Council is on the lower end of the expenses per head of municipal population indicating improved capacity to provide services. Future increases in expenditure is expected in line with projected fluctuations in CPI levels.

Description: Infrastructure per head of municipal population
Variation: The increase of 3.7% primarily relates to a higher capital works program and increase in municipal population over the 12-month period by 4.5% impacting the final result.

Description: Population density per length of road
Variation: With the growth in population from the previous year, this indicator has in turn increased.

Description: Own-source revenue per head of municipal population
Variation: Own source revenue in 2023/24 increased by 3.2%. Statutory Fees and Fines increased compared to 2022/23. Income from parking infringments and court fines income, as a result of resuming enforcement after previous years impacted by COVID-19 restrictions. User fees increased due to Council services and leisure and aquatic facilities returning to full capacity. Income increased in leisure and aquatic facilities by $2.3M, waste charges by $0.5M, other fees and charges by $1.4M compared to 2022/23. Municipal population increased by 4.5% which has also contributed to the $949 result.

Description: Recurrent grants per head of municipal population
Variation: This ratio decreased by 31.2% over 2022/23 levels with an overall decrease in recurrent grant income of $6.4M. This is mainly due to not receiving the 2024/25 Financial Assistance Grants in June 2024 as expected. Municipal population increased by 4.5%.

Description: Relative Socio-Economic Disadvantage
Variation: A score of 9 suggests City of Monash has low levels of disadvantage.

Description: Percentage of staff turnover
Variation: Council experienced 135 terminations of permanent employees within 2023/24 financial year.  This was a reduction of four terminations against the previous financial year.  Of the 135 terminations, 100 were voluntary including 5 retirements.  Of the 35 non voluntary terminations this is mainly made up of fixed term contracts ending as per agreement, as well as 10 redundancies (largely due to exiting regional aged care assessments as part of the Federal Government’s Aged Care Reform) and 6 dismissals.  Council's turnover is on par with the industry with ranges from 14% to 20% turnover.

Description: Cost of library service per population
Variation: CPI was a significant factor which increased  the cost of providing the service.

Description: Health inspections of aquatic facilities
Variation: Aquatic facilities were inspected in accordance with statutory requirements.

Description: Utilisation of aquatic facilities
Variation: Annual aquatic visitation across all leisure centres continued to increase. The growth is attributed to a rise in health and wellness memberships and learn-to-swim programs, and concerted efforts to increase membership retention.

Description: Cost of aquatic facilities
Variation: Council's aquatic facilities are provided at a very low subsidy to the community. While in 2023/24 visitations increased, higher utility costs offset the increased income resulting in a slightly greater cost to deliver the service compared to 2022/23.

Description: Time taken to action animal management requests
Variation: Council has maintained the improvement in the time taken to action requests due to ongoing process and administrative improvements to the management of the service.

Description: Animals reclaimed
Variation: The rate of animals reclaimed has been steadily increasing due to ongoing process improvements.

Description: Animals rehomed
Variation: The rehoming of animals has been consistent following the significant improvement achieved since 2020/21.

Description: Cost of animal management service per population
Variation: There was an increase in non-direct costs associated with delivering the service, particularly associated with housing collected animals.

Description: Animal management prosecutions
Variation: There was one prosecution for animal management in which Council was successful.

Description: Time taken to action food complaints
Variation: Ongoing process improvements saw a reduction on the time taken to action food complaints.

Description: Food safety assessments
Variation: All food safety assessments were completed.

Description: Cost of food safety service
Variation: Council’s food safety service runs efficiently and further improvements were made to the assessment process to keep cost effectiveness, despite CPI having a significant impact on service delivery.

Description: Critical and major non-compliance outcome notifications
Variation: All major and non-compliant follow-up inspections were completed.

Description: Food safety samples
Variation: The legislated requirement for food sampling was fully met.

Description: Council decisions made at meetings closed to the public
Variation: Fewer Council decisions were required to be made confidentially compared to 2022/23. All were in accordance with the Act.

Description: Satisfaction with community consultation and engagement
Variation: Council has received strong engagement by the community across various matters throughout the year. Resourcing has been allocated to the conduct and promotion of a greater number of engagement activities, and a number of Community Advisory Panels were convened to undertake deliberative engagement.

Description: Councillor attendance at council meetings
Variation: Attendance by Councillors remained high.

Description: Cost of elected representation
Variation: Cost of the governance service per Councillor remained steady. The lower unit cost in 2023/24 is attributed to less training and development in Councillors' final year of term.

Description: Satisfaction with council decisions
Variation: Satisfaction with Council decisions increased by two percentage points, reflecting Council's ongoing work to actively and publicly represent community interests on a number of important matters and advocacy issues.

Description: Recently purchased library collection
Variation: There was an increase in the size of the library collection, including at Flemington Library following the redevelopment and expansion there.

Description: Loans per head of population
Variation: This result sits in the middle of the range and represents strong interest in library resources by the community. The redevelopment of the Flemington Library (and temporary operation at a smaller satellite venue) over three months impacted the number of loans.

Description: Library membership
Variation: Utilisation of libraries remains strong. This is despite significant improvement works taking place at two libraries since 2021/22, which have impacted branch access and availability for some users.

Description: Library visits per head of population
Variation: The library service is well used by residents. However visitation to libraries was impacted by redevelopment of the Flemington Library over three months. While the service was continued at a pop-up facility its smaller size meant that not as many users could be accommodated.

Description: Infant enrolments in the MCH service
Variation: All infants are enrolled from birth notifications received. The result was greater than 100% due to a number of infants enrolled in the service following notification by domiciliary services and families moving into the municipality. This is a normal occurrence. The result demonstrates a consistently high level of engagement.

Description: Cost of the MCH service
Variation: Less reliance on casual staff was the main factor contributing to the decrease in cost for the service.

Description: Participation in the MCH service
Variation: Participation in the maternal and child health service remained steady. The ongoing challenge of staff attrition/turnover is a factor inhibiting growth in participation.

Description: Participation in the MCH service by Aboriginal children
Variation: Participation in maternal and child health services by Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander children increased by nearly 5%.

Description: Participation in 4-week Key Age and Stage visit
Variation: There were more infants in special care / extended hospital stays than past years, and a higher than average number of stillbirths which impacted the number of infants eligible for the Key Age and Stage visit at 4 weeks. Additionally there was a proportion of families seeing private midwives who did not engage with the service until after 4 weeks of age. Delivery of the service was impacted by staff availability.

Description: Sealed local road requests
Variation: Major flooding significantly damaged sealed local roads which led to a high number of requests for repair. Despite this, Council's performance in this service has still met community expectations well.

Description: Sealed local roads maintained to condition standards
Variation: All local roads were maintained to condition standards, ensuring that none fell below the renewal intervention level.

Description: Cost of sealed local road reconstruction
Variation: Roads were prioritised for reconstruction in accordance with Council’s Road Management Plan and Asset Management Plan. Long-term supply contracts and large-scale projects generated economies of scale within the program, resulting in a reduced unit rate of delivery compared to previous years.

Description: Cost of sealed local road resealing
Variation: Roads were prioritised for resealing in accordance with Council’s Road Management Plan and Asset Management Plan. Whilst large scale projects generated some economies of scale, the need for thicker pavements and the need to provide greater service levels to more major roads resulted in an increased unit rate of delivery in 2023/24.

Description: Satisfaction with sealed local roads
Variation: Council has had an increased focus on road repairs and quality improvements over recent years.

Description: Time taken to decide planning applications
Variation: Council continued to focus on improving systems to enhance the efficiency of workflows to reduce the time taken to decide planning applications.

Description: Planning applications decided within required time frames
Variation: Decisions were made on 821 applications (both Standard and VicSmart applications). Over 97% of VicSmart applications and over 80% of Standard applications were decided within the assessment timeframes of 10 and 60 days respectively.

Description: Cost of statutory planning service
Variation: The increase can be attributed to a reduction in the number of planning applications received compared to the previous year, resulting in a higher per application cost.

Description: Council planning decisions upheld at VCAT
Variation: A total of 27 appeals were recorded, of which only one was set aside. Ten appeals (37%) were resolved via the consent of parties, a further three (11%) were withdrawn/struck out and the remaining 14 were heard by the Tribunal.

Description: Kerbside collection bins missed
Variation: Missed bin complaints decreased due to efforts to improve reporting, data analysis to understand issues, and the implementation of corrective actions.

Description: Cost of kerbside garbage bin collection service
Variation: Due to the introduction of the Food Organics Garden Organics universal service there was less landfill generated resulting in a lower disposal cost.

Description: Cost of kerbside recyclables collection service
Variation: The cost of the service has remained relatively stable. Efforts were made in early 2024 to educate community on correct recycling practice, as the cost of the service can be reduced through minimising disposal costs associated with contamination of recyclables.

Description: Kerbside collection waste diverted from landfill
Variation: More waste was diverted from landfill resulting from the introduction of the universal Food Organics and Garden Organics (FOGO) collection service in the latter part of the financial year.

Description: Expenses per property assessment
Variation: The increase is due to external factors including the increase in the cost of materials to deliver on infrastructure renewal and services to the community. In addition, in 2021/22 there was a change in Leisure Facilities on how program costs were to be reported which resulted in an increase in expenses however the was a corresponding increase in user fees revenue.

Description: Average rate per property assessment
Variation: The variation is due to an increase in the number of property assessments.

Description: Current assets compared to current liabilities
Variation: The variation is due to the increase in trade and other payables and provision for employee leave entitlements. The increase in the provision for employee leave entitlements is due to a reduction in staff turnover. There was also less funds held in term deposits reflecting a decrease in Other Financial Assets.

Description: Unrestricted cash compared to current liabilities
Variation: The variation is due to an increase in the cash and cash equivalents as less funds were invested in Other Financial assets in FY24 compared to FY23.

Description: Loans and borrowings compared to rates
Variation: The variation is due to borrowings proposed as part of the  2023/24 adopted budget of $16 million not being called upon. The percentage increase in future years is due to the increase in the forecasted borrowing amount.

Description: Loans and borrowings repayments compared to rates
Variation: The variation is due to borrowings proposed as part of the  2023/24 adopted budget of $16 million not being called upon. The percentage increase in future years is due to the increase in the forecasted borrowing amount.

Description: Non-current liabilities compared to own source revenue
Variation: The variation is due to an increase in rates and charges user fees. The percentage increase in future years is due to the increase in the forecasted borrowing amount.

Description: Asset renewal and upgrade compared to depreciation
Variation: The variation to the Target percentage is predominately due to a reduced renewal and upgrade spend caused by a delay in the completion of capital projects. The projects that were delayed will be completed in 2024/25.

Description: Adjusted underlying surplus (or deficit)
Variation: The variation is due to a decrease in operating grants. The percentage increase in future years is due to forecast increases in the operating surplus.

Description: Rates compared to adjusted underlying revenue
Variation: The variation is due to a decrease in operating grants resulting in a higher adjusted underlying revenue in 2023/24.

Description: Rates compared to property values
Variation: The variation is predominately due to an increase in the revenue for general residential rates and waste charges.

Description: Expenses per head of municipal population
Variation: The trend of increasing costs is reflective of a range of factors including a return to service delivery following the pandemic, continued emergency recovery efforts following the Maribyrnong River flood, and increasing labour and supply costs.

However, the average municipal score masks that there are localities in Moonee Valley that have higher levels of socio-economic disadvantage.

Description: Percentage of staff turnover
Variation: Moorabool Shire Council has invested significantly in its attraction and retention activities and culture change program. This has resulted in a working environment (and accompanying terms and conditions) that is quickly entering the destination employer category. As such, our people have been more included to stay with Council and this has been reflected in our turnover rates.

Description: Health inspections of aquatic facilities
Variation: Shire authorised officers carried out 12 inspections across Council’s three aquatic facilities: six at Yawa Aquatic Centre, four at Pelican Park Recreation Centre and two at Crib Point Pool.

Description: Utilisation of aquatic facilities
Variation: The increase in the utilisation of our aquatic centres from 2021 is attributed to strong attendance numbers, an additional aquatic facility and four full trading quarters without any COVID closures, capacity restrictions, or significant facility maintenance/repair closures.

Description: Cost of aquatic facilities
Variation: Despite receiving a similar number of visits to last year, an increase in revenue allowed us to achieve a lower cost-per-visit ratio.

Description: Time taken to action animal management requests
Variation: An 82% increase in animal requests from last year has resulted in an increase in the time taken to action animal management requests.

Description: Animals reclaimed
Variation: This year’s result is mainly due to a 45% decrease in animals collected, with owners only reclaiming 190 of the 459 animals collected over the year.

Description: Animals rehomed
Variation: The increase in animals rehomed is mainly due to fewer animals collected and a change in the calculation, which has been updated to remove animals that have been reclaimed from the calculation. Of the unclaimed pets collected, we were able to rehome over half.

Description: Cost of animal management service per population
Variation: The increase against last year is due to an increase in salaries due to a staff position at the animal shelter being filled, paid maternity leave and the use of external contractors.

Description: Animal management prosecutions
Variation: Council is committed to protecting the safety of the community and the health and safety of animals on the Peninsula by prosecuting only when appropriate and necessary. Council prosecuted 25 Animal Management matters over the year.

Description: Time taken to action food complaints
Variation: Council continues to prioritise food complaints and action as soon as possible.

Description: Food safety assessments
Variation: We continue to inspect and approve every food premise before trading and ensure that all food premises on the Peninsula receive an annual food safety assessment. However, a small number of newly established premises that began trading in late 2023 were not assessed in time.

Description: Cost of food safety service
Variation: The decrease in the cost of the food safety service from 2022 is primarily due to the realignment of internal costs which now reflect the resources allocated to our food safety service.

Description: Critical and major non-compliance outcome notifications
Variation: To ensure the safety of our community, we continue to prioritise food safety compliance programs across the Peninsula. Our follow-up on critical and major notifications result remains high and is consistent with previous years.

Description: Food safety samples
Variation: New for 2023-2024, the Food Safety Samples measure shows Council's commitment to food safety on the Peninsula. Of the 258 food samples required, we were able to obtain 224 for analysis.

Description: Council decisions made at meetings closed to the public
Variation: Thirteen decisions were made at meetings closed to the public. Of these, five related to private commercial information, being information provided by a business that if released would unreasonably expose the business to disadvantage; three were in regards to personal information, being information which if released would result in the unreasonable disclosure of information about any person or their personal affairs; three decisions related to Council business information, being information that would prejudice the Council's position in commercial negotiations; two were in regards to legal privileged information, being information to which legal professional privilege applies and one was in regards to land use planning, being information that if released is likely to encourage speculation in land values.

Description: Satisfaction with community consultation and engagement
Variation: Research conducted by an independent company that measures the opinions of local people in the community showed satisfaction levels increased 17 index points compared to last year, surpassing our target of 52 for the year.

Description: Councillor attendance at council meetings
Variation: Councillor attendance has experienced a decline from 2021 as a result of our transition back to in-person meetings and an increase in unplanned Council Meetings throughout the year.

Description: Cost of elected representation
Variation: The overall cost of elected representation has increased due to higher Councillor allowances, which are set by the Victorian Independent Remuneration Tribunal and Superannuation rates as per the Australian Taxation Office guidelines.

Description: Satisfaction with council decisions
Variation: Research conducted by an independent company that measures the opinions of local people in the community, showed satisfaction levels increased 18 index points compared to last year.

Description: Recently purchased library collection
Variation: The decrease from 2022 is mainly due to our new Management Collection System, which helps us better manage our library collection. This system helped identify titles that were not being used or no longer relevant, leading to fewer items in our collection.

Description: Loans per head of population
Variation: New for 2023-2024, the Library loans per population measure assesses the number of library loans per person to evaluate community utilisation. The result falls within Local Government Victoria’s expected range of 4 to 8.

Description: Library membership
Variation: New for the 2023-2024 period, the Library membership measure calculates the percentage of Mornington Peninsula residents who are registered library members, which will help us understand the demand for our library service. The expected range for this percentage, as set by Local Government Victoria, is between 20-40%.

Description: Library visits per head of population
Variation: New for 2023-2024, the Library visits per population indicator measures the municipal population’s participation and uptake of our Library service. The result is within the Local Government Victoria’s expected range of 2-4.

Description: Infant enrolments in the MCH service
Variation: This year’s result is largely consistent with previous years. Our community’s uptake of the service remains high, demonstrating the importance of maternal and child health services for families with children aged 0-6 years.

Description: Cost of the MCH service
Variation: The decrease from 2023 is mainly due to a reduction in casual Maternal Child Health salaries and wages to cover permanent staff on leave and less venue and equipment hire.

Description: Participation in the MCH service
Variation: Participation in the Maternal Child Health service remains consistent but is down slightly from 2021.

Description: Participation in the MCH service by Aboriginal children
Variation: Our full-year result is down from 2023 due to a decrease in the number of Aboriginal children enrolled and attending our Maternal Child Health service at least once in the year. There is always some participation variation as children, depending on their birthday, may or may not be eligible for a Key Age and Stage appointment at the end of December. Additionally, some families are choosing to attend First Peoples' Health services in Frankston, an Aboriginal led health service.

Description: Participation in 4-week Key Age and Stage visit
Variation: We closely monitor client attendance and proactively reach out to clients who have missed their Key Age and Stages appointments. As a result, community participation in 4-week Key Age and Stage (KAS) visits remains high but has decreased slightly compared to previous years. This decline can be attributed to staffing issues, with 5 permanent staff taking unplanned long-term leave, which impacted our service provision. We have since hired additional casual nurses to address this.

Description: Sealed local road requests
Variation: The decrease in the number of requests for sealed local roads this year is due to below-average rainfall. Total rainfall on the Peninsula for the year was approximately 70% of the last 8-year average. Lower rainfall results in significantly fewer road pavement defects. As a result, we received 1,538 requests, which is a 56% decrease from the previous high of 3,475 requests received during the same period last year.

Description: Sealed local roads maintained to condition standards
Variation: Of the 1,392 kilometres of sealed local roads across the Shire we maintained 1,392 kilometres within condition standards, beating our target for the year.

Description: Cost of sealed local road reconstruction
Variation: There were no road rehabilitation works from July 2023 to June 2024 because resources were redirected to our Road Resealing Program for 2023-24.

Description: Cost of sealed local road resealing
Variation: The rise in the cost of maintaining local roads is due to a greater percentage of micro-surfacing work, compared with sprayed seal work, carried out this year. This has led to a higher reseal unit rate per square metre. The unit rate cost can vary significantly depending on the type of treatment and preliminary patching works required.

Description: Satisfaction with sealed local roads
Variation: Research conducted by an independent company that measures the opinions of local people in the community, showed satisfaction levels increased 18 index points compared to last year.

Description: Time taken to decide planning applications
Variation: Although we received 9% fewer applications compared to last year, additional resources, process improvements and increased staff experience have all contributed to shorter processing times of applications.

Description: Planning applications decided within required time frames
Variation: Although we were able to increase our result compared to the previous year, we didn't meet our target of 60%. This was mainly due to a backlog of applications and staff secondments within the planning department. Despite there being a decrease in the number of applications received, gaps in staffing knowledge affected our ability to process applications within the desired timeframes to reach our target.

Description: Cost of statutory planning service
Variation: Since we addressed staff shortages last year and received fewer expected applications this year, the cost of the service is stabilising and comparable to 2023 and pre-COVID results.

Description: Council planning decisions upheld at VCAT
Variation: The slight decrease against last year is mainly due to a change in how the measure is calculated - it now includes Consent Orders, which is a decision or direction by VCAT that gives effect to an agreement that has been reached between parties.

Description: Kerbside collection bins missed
Variation: As with last year, this year's results are primarily due to the return to our normal collection schedule and improved reporting. We introduced additional categories in our reporting to ensure we captured all missed bins.

Description: Cost of kerbside garbage bin collection service
Variation: The increase in our kerbside garbage collection service from last year is mainly due to annual adjustments to the contract and an approximate 2.7% increase in the landfill levy from 2022-23, which has seen the cost gradually increase.

Description: Cost of kerbside recyclables collection service
Variation: Due to an adjustment in the contract, we saw a slight decrease in the cost of the service compared to last year.

Description: Kerbside collection waste diverted from landfill
Variation: We surpassed our 59% target despite a 6% decrease in kerbside recycling materials received during the year. The reduction in materials is attributed to the introduction of the Container Deposit Scheme launched on November 1, 2023.

Description: Expenses per property assessment
Variation: Council always seeks to deliver the highest quality services in the most efficient way and has contained expenditure per property assessment through its goal of ongoing savings. The increase in 2024 is largely attributable to CPI, indexation of the Shire's contract and an increase in our building maintenance.

Description: Average rate per property assessment
Variation: Council's rates, our primary source of income that delivers essential services to our community, is limited by the rate cap under the Fair Go Rates System, which was set at 3.50% for 2023-24. Supplementary income is 0.8% of the total rates revenue in 2024, which is the growth of our rates income in 2024.

Description: Current assets compared to current liabilities
Variation: Our current assets have remained in line with 2023 due to cash and term deposits being kept at similar levels with delayed expenditure for capital works and high interest rates. There has been an increase in working capital due to Current Liabilities reducing as a result of a $9 million Contract and Other Liabilities being recognised in 2024 as non-current.

Description: Unrestricted cash compared to current liabilities
Variation: The negative result has arisen as Council has allocated cash to term deposits in order to maximise the return to Council funds. The term deposits are reported as Other Financial Assets and the total of $100.6M at 30 June 2024. If the term deposits were considered Cash and Cash Equivalents, then the Unrestricted cash ratio would have been 111%.

Description: Loans and borrowings compared to rates
Variation: No new loans drawn during the year and $2.9M principal loan re-payments, along with the rates revenue increase resulted in this ratio reducing.

Description: Loans and borrowings repayments compared to rates
Variation: An increase in rate revenue and a reduction in principal loan balances have resulted in the reduction of this ratio. Borrowings are forecast for 2025 leading to the future year increase.

Description: Non-current liabilities compared to own source revenue
Variation: Own Source revenue has increased by 9% due to rate revenue, higher usage or waste collection services and improved performance of recreation and aquatic facilities. Non-current liabilities have increased slightly, overall maintaining the indebtedness ratio in 2024.

Description: Asset renewal and upgrade compared to depreciation
Variation: Asset renewal and upgrade are driven by the condition assessment of assets and varies year on year. Due to current financial pressure the capital works program is focused on renewal projects with a reduction in new asset expenditure.

Description: Adjusted underlying surplus (or deficit)
Variation: The increase from 2023 is due to the 5% increase in income, compared to 2% increase in expenditure, however due to approximately $4 million in operating projects being carried forward into 2025, it will impact on the adjusted underlying surplus in future years.

Description: Rates compared to adjusted underlying revenue
Variation: Although we have grown other revenue (own-source revenue) Council revenue is still largely dependent on rate revenue to fund services and capital works.

Description: Rates compared to property values
Variation: Property values decreased this year on the Mornington Peninsula for the first time in a number of years, falling below the rate cap.

Description: Expenses per head of municipal population
Variation: Council always aims to provide high-quality efficient services while controlling expenditure through ongoing cost savings. The 2024 increase is primarily due to the Consumer Price Index (CPI), contract indexation, and increased staff costs with a decrease in the staff turnover rate.

Description: Infrastructure per head of municipal population
Variation: Our investment in Infrastructure has been impacted by the delivery of the Capital Works Program ($59 million) and the revaluation of infrastructure assets.

Description: Population density per length of road
Variation: A small rise in the municipal population has resulted in a slight increase against last year.

Description: Own-source revenue per head of municipal population
Variation: Our growth in own-source revenue is in line with budget expectations and has been driven by the rate cap and supplementaries during the year.

Description: Recurrent grants per head of municipal population
Variation: Recurrent grants have significantly decreased in 2024 due to the timing of the financial assistance grant for 2024 being paid in 2023 and the 2025 grant being paid in the 2025 financial year.

Description: Relative Socio-Economic Disadvantage
Variation: Mornington Peninsula's Relative Socio-Economic Disadvantage Index from the 2021 Census was in the eighth decile. The first decile indicates the most disadvantaged and the tenth decile indicates the least disadvantaged.

Description: Percentage of staff turnover
Variation: The turnover rate of 14% represents a decrease of 2.3% from the previous year. This figure encompasses all turnover, including staff whose employment ended due to scheduled contract terminations, involuntary redundancies, and terminations. The highest turnover rate for the financial year occurred in the last quarter, which saw 10 departures linked to the cessation of a service.

Description: Cost of library service per population
Variation: In 2022, we converted most of our casual staff to part-time employees, which helped stabilise our costs. However, this year we have experienced a small increase as we filled vacancies from 2023.

Description: Health inspections of aquatic facilities
Variation: All pools were inspected and water quality tested during the financial year.

Description: Utilisation of aquatic facilities
Variation:
A decrease in attendance of less than 1% compared to 2022/2023. It has been identified, that some facilities did not accurately record additional family members entering on a family/ family concession membership (only counted as 1 attendee, while up to 4 were able to attend on the pass). Actual attendances are estimated to be higher than recorded at some facilities when reviewing family membership passes sold and prior year averages. 
In addition there was a run of days over 35 °C in the week prior to closing, in early March 2024. The pools were closed for 8 days through the season due to cold weather, however opening hours were extended 9 times due to warmer evenings, as per the weather policy.

Description: Cost of aquatic facilities
Variation:
There have been no additional costs this year, compared to previous years. The four outdoor seasonal pools are managed by an external contractor.
The higher result is due to error in the recording of family member entries on the family season membership at some facilities (only counted as 1 attendee, while up to 4 were able to attend on the pass). This impacted the overall recording of attendances, with the estimated number of visits across the facilities higher than that of previous years.

Description: Time taken to action animal management requests
Variation: All Animal Management requests are actioned within 1-2 business days.

Description: Animals reclaimed
Variation: There has been a 8% decrease in animals reclaimed However, happily, there has also been a 27% decrease in surrender of dogs by the public compared to 2022/2023.

Description: Animals rehomed
Variation: Adoption/rehomed rates of cats improved dramatically with a 34% increase, compared to 2022/2023, while dog rehoming rate remained the same.

Description: Cost of animal management service per population
Variation: Costs have decreased by 16%, with a reduction in permanent staff during 2023/2024.

Description: Animal management prosecutions
Variation: No animal prosecutions were undertaken for 2023/2024.

Description: Time taken to action food complaints
Variation: All food complaint requests are actioned within 1-2 business days.

Description: Food safety assessments
Variation: Annual food safety assessments completed improved 10% compared to 2022.

Description: Cost of food safety service
Variation: While there has been an increase of 7% in the number of registered premises, there has only been a 3% increase in the cost of providing the service compared to 2022/2023.

Description: Critical and major non-compliance outcome notifications
Variation: Follow up for some premises was undertaken in the following calendar year (2024) and so do not meet the date parameters for this reporting period. Low and decreasing numbers of notifications received (37 in 2020, 13 in 2021, 11 in 2022, 4 in 2023), can skew the percentage change between years.

Description: Food safety samples
Variation: 92% of the required food samples were obtained and tested in 2023. This is a new indicator and so has no comparatives.

Description: Council decisions made at meetings closed to the public
Variation:
Eight resolutions were passed at closed Council meetings.
2022/2023 number of council resolutions made at all meetings was reported too high as accidently included July 2023 meeting in these figures. 2022/2023 result should have been 4.05 instead. This reduces the year on year variance to 101.56%.

Description: Satisfaction with community consultation and engagement
Variation: Council has worked hard to increase community consultation and engagement using a number of strategies including: media, briefings and streaming of Council Meetings on YouTube. Result has improved compared to 2022/2023 and is within 5.45% of target set.

Description: Councillor attendance at council meetings
Variation: Four Councillors were absent on six separate occasions.

Description: Cost of elected representation
Variation: Service costs increased by 5.5% compared to 2022/2023.

Description: Satisfaction with council decisions
Variation: A pleasing result reflecting how Council has endeavoured to raise public awareness of its decisions, meetings, and activities through media releases, live streaming of Council Meetings to the internet, and actively encouraging community involvement in projects via our online community engagement platform.

Description: Recently purchased library collection
Variation: Minor increase in library collection items purchased.

Description: Loans per head of population
Variation: New indicator for 2023/2024, that demonstrates the percentage of loans borrowed by the resident municipal population.

Description: Library membership
Variation: New indicator for 2023/2024, that demonstrates the percentage of the resident municipal population who are registered library members in 2023/2024.

Description: Library visits per head of population
Variation: New indicator for 2023/2024, that demonstrates the percentage of the resident municipal population who visit the library.

Description: Infant enrolments in the MCH service
Variation: All births were enrolled in the Maternal and Child Health service.

Description: Cost of the MCH service
Variation: There has been a 16% increase in service costs and a 10% increase in Maternal and Child Health nurse hours worked, compared to 2022/2023.

Description: Participation in the MCH service
Variation: Attendance decreased by 6.2% while enrolments decreased by 4.0% compared to 2022/2023.

Description: Participation in the MCH service by Aboriginal children
Variation: Low numbers of Aboriginal children enrolled (15 in 2020/2021, 16.5 in 2021/2022, 19 in 2022/2023, 17 in 2023/2024), can skew the percentage change between years.

Description: Participation in 4-week Key Age and Stage visit
Variation: A higher number of children were born in June (compared to 2022/2023) and were not eligible for the 4 week Key age and stage visit.

Description: Sealed local road requests
Variation: The number of local road customer requests received in 2023/2024 decreased compared to 2022/2023. This supports the improved customer satisfaction survey result received.

Description: Sealed local roads maintained to condition standards
Variation: The majority of sealed roads are in good condition, according to a recent survey of road conditions in 2020/2021. Result is stable compared to 2022/2023 and is within 0.03% of target set.

Description: Cost of sealed local road reconstruction
Variation: Road reconstruction unit rates vary depending on a number of factors, including project value, specifications, road length, width, and depth, material types, design criteria, and other related works such as minor drainage, shoulders, cut and fill, and resource availability. As a result, a rural council cannot avoid price fluctuations in road reconstruction projects. In comparison to the financial year 2022/2023, the unit rate nearly doubled in 2023/2024. Small projects are extremely expensive, which could be attributed to the project's scope and increased demand for civil contractors. However, the unit rate falls within the expected range.

Description: Cost of sealed local road resealing
Variation: Unit rates for road resealing are determined by a number of factors, including seal designs, road lengths, widths, aggregate sizes, material types, road functionalities, associated preparation work, available resources, and so on. As a result, a rural council cannot avoid price changes for road resurfacing projects. Because of the aforementioned factors, the unit rate decreased slightly from 2022/2023 to 2023/2024. However, the unit rate remains within the expected range.

Description: Satisfaction with sealed local roads
Variation: The 2023/2024 survey showed an improvement in customer satisfaction, which is also reflected in less customer requests received. Council is working hard to provide good services to residents.

Description: Time taken to decide planning applications
Variation: Decision timeframes have improved following significant recruitment undertaken.

Description: Planning applications decided within required time frames

Description: Time taken to action animal management requests
Variation: The number of requests received has remained relatively stable (3,703 requests in 2023/24 compared to 3,759 in 2022/23). Council facilitates and promotes customer self-service through our online portal, which has helped to decrease the number of requests received.  We continue to provide a responsive and high-quality service to our community.

Description: Animals reclaimed
Variation: Of the 225 animals collected from 1 July 2023 to 30 June 2024, 84 animals (37.3%) were reclaimed by their owners. Of the 225 animals collected, 55 (24.4%) had been surrendered by their owners. There has been an increase in surrendered animals. As surrendered animals will not be reclaimed, this has reduced Council's reclaim percentage. Council Officers make every effort to return pets to their owners. Pet owners are encouraged to register their pets with Council to ensure quick return.

Description: Animals rehomed
Variation: Animals rehomed is calculated as a percentage of all unclaimed animals collected. Of the 225 animals collected, 84 were reclaimed by owners (37.3%). Of the remaining 141 animals, 73 (51.8%) were rehomed. The number of foster carers has increased, reducing the strain on the shelter and increasing the number of adoptions. The definition in this measure has changed, and 2024 results do not include animals that have been reclaimed, which has impacted the results.

Description: Cost of animal management service per population
Variation: Despite an increase in fees from the Lost Dogs Home, the direct cost of Animal Management Services has decreased this year. Animal Management Officers have placed a greater emphasis on returning animals to their owners from the field, reducing ambulance costs and impound fees. The cost of service is operating within budget and is within the range of comparable Councils.

Description: Animal management prosecutions
Variation: Council achieved 100 per cent success rate on animal prosecutions through the Magistrates' Court of Victoria. All cases were thoroughly assessed to ensure accuracy of evidence prior to being submitted for prosecution.

Description: Time taken to action food complaints
Variation: The number of days between receipt and first response action for all food complaints has improved slightly compared to the previous year.

Description: Food safety assessments
Variation: All class 1 and 2 food premises with a food safety program  received an assessment by an Environmental Health Officer within the calendar year.

Description: Cost of food safety service
Variation: The cost per registered premises has increased due to an increase in employee costs and materials with minimal increase in the number of registered premises.

Description: Critical and major non-compliance outcome notifications

Description: Food safety samples
Variation: The number of food samples required for the calendar year were collected and submitted for analysis.

Description: Council decisions made at meetings closed to the public
Variation: Council has recently reviewed the process for designating information confidential, including decisions made at meetings closed to members of the public. Greater scrutiny is now applied to determine which information must be considered confidential. All confidentiality designations now require a reason explaining why the relevant legislation applies and consideration is given to when each matter can be made public. We also undertake a biannual review of confidential information to assess what can and should be released to the public.

Description: Satisfaction with community consultation and engagement
Variation:
Three rounds of the Neighbourhood Engagement Program have been delivered over the past 12 months, with participation rates increasing steadily over the year. This trend culminated in a 250% increase in participation from April 24 compared to March 23. 
We attribute the decline in this result to the number of high-profile, polarising topics that Council consulted on this year, including: Inkerman Street, St Kilda Triangle, Dog Off-Leash Guidelines and the Public Toilet Plan. 
Council will continue to improve our approach to community consultation and engagement, with the Engagement Policy review scheduled to commence once new councillors are onboarded.

Description: Councillor attendance at council meetings
Variation: There were 15 apologies received by Councillors during the 2023/24 financial year. Councillor Clark was on an approved leave of absence for two meetings, and Councillors Cunsolo and Sirakoff were on approved leaves of absence for one meeting each. All Councillors have the option to attend Council Meetings either in person or virtually. This contributes to a higher attendance rate at Council Meetings

Description: Cost of elected representation
Variation: The increased cost of elected representation in 2023/24 is mainly due to the increase in Councillor allowances – as determined by the Victorian Independent Renumeration Tribunal.

Description: Satisfaction with council decisions
Variation: Council's rating was lower than the Metropolitan group average, and marginally lower than the Statewide average. Although engagement programs for a number of key projects (such as Aged Care Reform) were thorough, and Council decisions reflected overarching community sentiment and officer recommendations, some initiatives greatly divided community opinion. Council will continue to focus on engagement, data analysis and reporting to support transparency and accountability, as well as improved decision making on behalf of the community.

Description: Recently purchased library collection
Variation: Collection spending was adjusted to meet increased demand for physical collection items, resulting in a 19% increase in new items purchased. The number of items older than 5 years has been reduced in line with industry standards.

Description: Loans per head of population
Variation: Loans of collection items increased by 18% in 2023/24. This figure reflects Council's implementation of auto-renewals, which increased convenience for patrons and enhanced customer experience. Our collection has also become more appealing due to the purchase of new material and best-selling authors.

Description: Library membership
Variation: The registration of new library members has increased 8%, from 8,947 in 2022/23 to 9,689 in 2023/24. This reflects a general increase in active users of library collections (across print and digital forms) and growth in the active users of library computers.

Description: Library visits per head of population
Variation: Library visits increased by 8% in 2023/24. This steady increase is due to relaxation of COVID-19 restrictions, more in-person programming and increased demand of in-person library services

Description: Infant enrolments in the MCH service
Variation: Enrolment in the MCH service is comparable to 2022/23. 2023/24 saw a small increase in enrolments and birth notifications. All families were contacted to engage them in the service. The total number of transfers of children out of Port Phillip decreased from 578 in 2022/23 to 492 in this reporting period.

Description: Cost of the MCH service
Variation: The total service cost of the Maternal and Child Health service is comparable to the 2022/23 financial year. The cost per hour increased in 2023/24 due to a reduction in the total hours worked in the service. This was due to a significant amount of unplanned leave within the service.

Description: Participation in the MCH service
Variation: The suite of programs offered to engage and follow up with families to encourage attendance was consistent with 2022/23. The Maternal and Child Health (MCH) Service experienced a small increase in the participation rate, reflecting an increased confidence in service engagement and a reduction in appointment non-attendance.

Description: Participation in the MCH service by Aboriginal children
Variation: The number of Aboriginal children who attended the MCH service at least once remained stable in 2023/24. A slight decrease in the number of Aboriginal children enrolled in the MCH service resulted in an overall increase in engagement as a percentage.

Description: Participation in 4-week Key Age and Stage visit
Variation: A decrease in the number of infants attending the 4-week visit compared to 2022/23, combined with an increase in birth notifications, resulted in a lower attendance rate at the 4-week key age and stage visits. Overall, 872 4-week key age and stage visits were conducted. All families were contacted following receipt of birth notices to engage them in the service. Contributing factors to this decrease include families choosing alternative support (such as private midwives) until the baby is six weeks of age to meet their specific/cultural needs, and families moving to another municipality.

Description: Sealed local road requests
Variation: We have seen an increase in customer requests relating to road conditions (despite a reported increase in road conditions). We field numerous customer requests relating to state-owned roads which are in deteriorating condition. Further work is required to be able to extract these requests from our reported figures.

Description: Sealed local roads maintained to condition standards
Variation: Our last assessment of condition was 94%. We have since fully upgraded two roads, which provided an amended result of 95.11%, exceeding Council’s target for 2023/24.

Description: Cost of sealed local road reconstruction
Variation: In 2023/24, two full-depth road reconstruction projects were undertaken, increasing costs significantly.

Description: Cost of sealed local road resealing
Variation: The reduced cost of sealed local road resurfacing is primarily due to lower contracting costs.

Description: Satisfaction with sealed local roads
Variation: Satisfaction with sealed local roads was above target. Council still has a large number of development projects, along with associated utility works, causing disruptions to the community with noise, road closure and congestion.

Description: Time taken to decide planning applications
Variation: Due to State Government planning reforms to fast-track minor permit processes, Council processed a higher number of VicSmart (fast-track) applications in the last financial year.  The increase in the number of less complex applications has resulted in a reduction in median number of days.

Description: Planning applications decided within required time frames
Variation: Council has increased the number of decisions made within the statutory timeframes. Over the past 12 months there has been significant staff turnover which has impacted timely service delivery. A plan is in place to actively manage the timeliness of decision making.

Description: Cost of statutory planning service
Variation: The results for this measure have been affected by an error in reporting in 2022/23 associated with transitioning to new software, which lead to double counting of some applications where the initial application type was incorrect. Data for 2022/23 and 2023/24 has now been reconciled. The actual variance in 2023/24 is a 5.5% decrease in cost (from $3,801.31 in 2022/23 to $3,593.37 in 2023/24).

Description: Council planning decisions upheld at VCAT
Variation: The number of planning decisions upheld at VCAT in 2023/24 continues to exceed Council's target of 70 per cent and is above the average of most other municipalities. The percentage is less than last financial year due to some applications being remitted to Council for decisions following State Government Amendment VC243, which meant that the Tribunal did not have jurisdiction to determine some appeals.

Description: Kerbside collection bins missed
Variation: The increase in missed kerbside collection bins is due to the transition to a new kerbside collections contract from 1 July. This resulted in a spike in missed bins in July and August (192 and 44.59 missed bins per 10,000, respectively) This trend resolved over the following months: in May and June the number of missed bins was down to 9 per 10,000 bins.

Description: Cost of kerbside garbage bin collection service
Variation: The cost of the garbage kerbside collection service has reduced in 2023/24 due to the commencement of a new collection contract.

Description: Cost of kerbside recyclables collection service
Variation: The cost of the recycling kerbside collection service has reduced in 2023/24 due to the commencement of a new collection contract. Council expects the cost will reduce further in 2024/25 due to commencement of a new recycling processing contract from 1 July 2024.

Description: Kerbside collection waste diverted from landfill
Variation: There has been an increase in landfill diversion from 2022/23 with the Food Organics and Garden Organics (FOGO) service rollout continuing into 2023/24. The rollout experienced some delays, and the service expansion to multi-unit dwellings was completed in March 2024. FOGO diversion rates started at 30% in July ahead of significant improvements throughout the year, with rates between 38% and 40% from December onwards. We anticipate that diversion rates will continue to increase as residents become more accustomed to this new service.

Description: Expenses per property assessment
Variation: The increase in expenses from prior year has impacted this ratio. This has been caused by ongoing inflationary pressures as well as additional costs in the wind up of some aged care services.  During the financial year Council transferred ownership of a parcel of land for community housing purposes resulting in a significant loss on disposal of assets due to the asset being written off.  This ratio is expected to increase in future years in line with CPI.  Future year ratios differ from the 2024/25 long term financial plan indicators due to a difference in calculation.

Description: Average rate per property assessment
Variation: This is consistent with prior year and expeceted to increase into the future in line with CPI.  Future year ratios differ from the 2024/25 long term financial plan indicators due to a difference in calculation.

Description: Current assets compared to current liabilities
Variation: Council continues to comfortably meet its short tem financial commitments. This ratio has increased slighty due to deposits paid for strategic land purchases for public open space.  In addition we continue to hold high short term cash as a result of delays in project spend with no signicficant increase in our liabilites.  We forecast a decline in this ratio in future years as a we draw down on our cash and financial assets to fund the delivery of our long term project portfolio ($110 million 2024/25, $84 million 2025/26).

Description: Unrestricted cash compared to current liabilities
Variation: The unrestricted cash ratio has increased from prior year due to higher cash on hand being available for operating purposes. Council continued to place a greater portion of cash in longer term investments that attract greater return. They are not included in the ratio  Council has a $144 million balanced portfolio with investment maturities timed to achieve our fossil free and rate of return targets. The cash and investment balance has $80 million of restricted cash to enable Council to fund the completion of projects in future years and ensure a strong financial to meet its obligations (evidenced in the working capital ratio).  Future year ratios differ from the 2024/25 long term financial plan indicators due to a difference in calculation.

Description: Loans and borrowings repayments compared to rates
Variation: Council have no current borrowings and no future borrowing plans.

Description: Non-current liabilities compared to own source revenue

In 2023/24 Council entered into a new significant waste management service contract that included exclusive use of heavy plants and trucks. This result is still low indicating that we can easily meet our financial obligations.

Description: Asset renewal and upgrade compared to depreciation
Variation:
Council spent $38 million on community assets during the 2023/24 financial year. $27 million were renewal and upgrade expenditure which represented 118% on depreciation. 
This ratio increased by 22% on 2022/23 due to greater amount of works completed in 23/24.
It is lower than the budgeted ratio of 199%, mainly due to deferred project spend in building, parks and open space. 
That said, the 2023/24 result indicates appropriate asset management as Council’s investment on renewing and upgrading our assets exceed depreciation.  This will increase in future years as we deliver our significant portfolio program.

Variation: This has decreased due to a reduced operating surplus in 2023/24 resulting from lower recurrent government grants as $3 million of funds from the Victoria Grants Commission were received in advance in the prior year. We expect this to improve in future financial years as grant timing will be consistent and no asset transfers are forecast.
